BLOCKED: G6.ESTOP_FAILED. Last gate run (2026-11-05, backend fake): G1-G5 pass, G6 fail, G7 pass, G8 pass, G9 skip. The G6 finding is: mhs.safety.estop: status failed, MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED: the device reports that its safe state was not reached; the latch stays engaged; retrying in the background (estop 'engaged', expected engaged or software_only). The pinned clone exposes no acknowledged stop for either cmd_vel topic. The two Gazebo differential-drive plugins only subscribe to the relative cmd_vel topic and publish odom (turtlebot3_burger1.gazebo.xacro:51-55, turtlebot3_burger2.gazebo.xacro:51-55); the shipped C++ node only advertises geometry_msgs::Twist on a configurable cmd_vel topic and subscribes to the relative scan and odom topics (turtlebot3_drive.cpp:42-57). No std_srvs, SetBool, Trigger or stop service/action is declared anywhere in the clone. The move_base action topics are remapped (move_base1.launch:38-56, move_base2.launch:38-56), but the clone contains no move_base_msgs/MoveBaseAction declaration, so the action cannot be a source-backed binding, and action cancellation is not a safe stop. RosDriver therefore reports the software latch and refuses to claim a safe state; a zero-velocity publication is transmission-only and is not an acknowledged stop. Adding a fake-only stop, a topic safe-state action, or an invented service would falsify the native contract; removing the cmd_vel commands would drop the primary motion control and violate the primary-interface requirement. This is HELPER_MISSING: the RosDriver can express the publications and observations but has no genuine upstream stop for this actuating profile. Scope: two TurtleBot3 Burger agents tb3_0 and tb3_1; cmd_vel publications and 360-sample scan/odom reads; R0 in simulated mode because the endpoints affect only Gazebo state. The fake is a ROS-free contract fake, F0, no physics; the scan/odom values are placeholders and a command applies a placeholder pose increment so the publication has an observable state effect. site-limits.example.json is illustrative and must be replaced by the operator. The move_base goal action, /clock, TF and the map server are out of scope because the pinned clone does not declare their message types. No hardware or live ROS run is claimed; driver.lock.json reviewed_by remains null.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the two simulated TurtleBot3 Burgers are driven only through the Gazebo differential-drive plugins' relative cmd_vel subscriptions (turtlebot3_burger1/2.gazebo.xacro:51-55), the clone declares no service, action server or stop of any kind (no advertiseService, rospy.Service or action server in its sources or launch files), and a zero-velocity publication is transmission-only, so the cmd_vel commands have no acknowledged stop and the stock e-stop fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED with the latch held, as for mrpt/mvsim. Endpoints and types were checked (/tb3_0 and /tb3_1 cmd_vel, odom and scan as move_base1/2.launch name and remap them, 8-11 and 33-35; the 360-sample 5 Hz lasers, 104-121), the operator_required velocity bounds and example overlay are right, the nine package cases pass when run alone, and the stable digest is unchanged (sha256:75cc32720f532a6c90027ff841e16e21d24b83b49a0dc7156398b815183ef961). Imprecisions left for whoever unblocks it: the fact on the drive node's 0.3 m/s and 1.5 rad/s constants cites only the two #define lines for its obstacle-avoidance clause and adds 'the clone states no signed cmd_vel envelope', while the clone's DWA planner files state max_vel_x 0.22, min_vel_x -0.22 and max_vel_theta 2.75 for move_base's own output (turtlebot3_navigation/multi_param/multi_param1/dwa_local_planner_params_burger.yaml:4-5, 14; operator_required stays the right bound for arbitrary publications); the e-stop case is named 'software_only' but asserts SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; and the /tb3_N plugin namespaces rest on gazebo_ros spawn_model behaviour outside the clone, corroborated only by the move_base remaps. The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings. For the human reviewer: Unblocking needs an acknowledged stop for the cmd_vel inputs (the clone has none; Gazebo's pause service lives in gazebo_ros, outside the clone). The navigation launch starts move_base1/2, which publish /tb3_0 and /tb3_1 cmd_vel whenever an RViz goal is active and would compete with MHS commands; the drive-node launch defaults to /cmd_vel and does not. The README's second goal topic /tb3_2/move_base_simple/goal names a robot the launch never spawns (tb3_0 and tb3_1).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Repaired from blocked (HELPER_MISSING) to pass under the user's decision of 2026-11-05 (a stop may cite a locally cloned companion repository at a pinned commit). The card now declares two reviewed companions (registry override companion-sources.json): gazebo_ros_pkgs at cd9cc952 (gazebo_ros 2.9.3, ROS 1 Noetic) and gazebo-classic at b22c6e15 (Gazebo 11.15.1), profile ros1-noetic-gazebo11, with version evidence on both sides that gate G1 re-checks (README.md:11-14 ROS Noetic and GAzebo 11, turtlebot3_gazebo package.xml:17 catkin, multi_turtlebot3_closeworld2.launch:16-23 empty_world.launch; gazebo_ros CHANGELOG.rst:5-7 Noetic 2.9.3, gazebo_dev package.xml:23-24 gazebo11). The e-stop is /gazebo/pause_physics (gazebo_ros_api_plugin.cpp:492-498; pausePhysics calls SetPaused(true), 1725-1729), confirmed only by the read-back /gazebo/get_physics_properties with pause == true (383-389; res.pause = IsPaused(), 1489); a failed pause, a failed read-back (a non-ODE engine) or pause false is SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held. The declared re-enable x-cap.mortezaaliyari.resume.v1 (CORE-086) first publishes a zero Twist on /tb3_0/cmd_vel and /tb3_1/cmd_vel, because the gazebo_ros differential-drive plugin stores the last command with no timeout (gazebo_ros_diff_drive.cpp:269-289, 324-340) and its queue runs while paused (342-349), then calls /gazebo/unpause_physics; the zeros are unacknowledged and move_base can publish new commands, both disclosed (SAFE-042). The odom and scan resource reads became four explicit read capabilities (silent while paused; a reset device must stay readable, TSAFE-001), and each cmd_vel receipt reports the values it sent. One pause stops both robots. The risk is now R2 for the two cmd_vel commands, the resume and the device (mobile-base transit, 04-safety.md section 2.1), replacing the author's R0: the relative cmd_vel topics would also drive a real TurtleBot3 behind the same rosbridge, as in the WPR package. Safe_state, the facts (now citing both companions), the fidelity gaps and facts.md say that the pause is the paused flag, not a measured standstill, that topic reads go silent while paused, and that the Gazebo GUI, a WorldControl step or any other client can advance or unpause the world. Files: driver.py, fake.py (a paused flag, the three Gazebo services, negative switches), test_driver.py, facts.md, driver.lock.json (companions), reference.json, REFERENCE.md, RESULT.json; task.json synced from the rebuilt card. All nine gates pass; evidence stays contract_checked on the fake only; no Gazebo, ROS graph or hardware ran; the R2 follows a claude-sonnet-5-5 review (round 1).
